summary: Resolve a merged ticket as terminal from Git when no receipt exists

delivery.outcome: An adopter can resolve a merged ticket as terminal from Git when no receipt exists, so the active set stops carrying merged work and the coordination rules that filter on it have a true set to reason over.
nonGoals: No change to the status-projection default, which the existing test defends as deliberately conservative.
No new conflict rule: deriving conflicts from allowedPaths was measured and yields thousands of findings on today's active sets.
No change to receipt-backed resolution, which already verifies by Git ancestry.

architecture.decision: Add git-ancestry as a second missingPolicy rather than reversing the default. A ticket directory on the target ref is the ancestry evidence the policy already declares, because a commit carrying only tracking carriers is refused, so the directory cannot be there without its delivery. Any branch for the same ticket outside the target keeps the ticket active, so a delivery still in flight is never resolved terminal.
interfaceChanges: registry.missingPolicy accepts git-ancestry in addition to status-projection; a resolution may now carry authority git-ancestry with reason delivery-on-target.
architecture.rollback: Return missingPolicy to a const and drop the derivation; adopters on the default were never affected.

validation.evidence: Measured 2026-09-09: four adopters projected 54, 65, 153 and 182 tickets active, with coding-agent's ticket-018, ticket-019 and ticket-111 merged into main while still reading IN_PROGRESS. On the same repository the two policies resolve 53 and 0 active, and an open pushed ticket-137 stays active under both.
